chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding the one who killed the hunting dog: 'It is evaluated [for compensation], and similarly [is the case for] the falcon, and similarly [is the case for] the sheep dog, and similarly [is the case for] the wall (guard) dog.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing a hunting dog or falcon in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'diya' or compensation for killing working animals, extending the principle of property valuation (qiwam) beyond livestock to include specialized animals like hunting dogs and falcons. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the economic value and utility of animals in daily life, treating them as distinct assets rather than mere creatures. The ruling underscores the legal continuity from Imam Ali (AS) regarding the protection of property rights in various forms of capital.
